Title: First page lists 5 offenders sorted alphabetically by last name
Steps:
1. Open the console.
2. Read the 5 rows of page 1.
3. Compare with GET api/offenders sorted by last name.
Expected result: Exactly 5 rows, alphabetical by last name (Amar, Azulay, Biton, Cohen, Dahan).

Title: Pager reaches every offender; pages = ceil(total/5)
URL / endpoint: UI {BASE_URL} pager "Page x of y (n results)"
Preconditions: Total offenders not a multiple of 5 (11 seeded).
Steps:
1. Open the console; read the pager.
2. Click Next › until disabled, collecting names.
3. Compare count with the results count.
Expected result: "Page 1 of 3 (11 results)"; all 11 offenders reachable, Peretz on page 3.

Title: API totalPages = ceil(total / pageSize) for many page sizes
Preconditions: Total offenders not a multiple of 5.
Steps:
1. Call the list endpoint for each page size.
2. Compare totalPages with ceil(total/pageSize).
Expected result: totalPages correct for every size (11 items: size 5 → 3, size 4 → 3, size 3 → 4).

Title: Following totalPages returns every offender exactly once
Preconditions: Total offenders not a multiple of 5.
Steps:
1. Read page 1 and totalPages.
2. Read pages 2..totalPages.
3. Collect ids.
Expected result: Collected ids = total, no duplicates.

Title: List response contract and last-name sort order
Steps:
1. Call the list endpoint.
2. Check fields and types.
3. Check sort order.
Expected result: items[], total, page, pageSize, totalPages (integers); total = items.length; sorted by last name.

Title: Out-of-range and invalid paging parameters handled gracefully
Steps: 1. Call the list endpoint with each parameter set.
Expected result: No 5xx. Page beyond the end → empty items with metadata; invalid values clamped to ≥ 1.

Title: Sorting is case-insensitive (lower-case last name sorts among A…)
Preconditions: Create an offender with last name "abergel".
Steps:
1. Create the offender.
2. Open the roster.
Expected result: "abergel" appears before "Amar", not after "Peretz".
Notes: Observed order: '', abergel, Amar, Azulay … (the '' entry is BUG-10 data).

Title: Search matches substrings of first name, last name and national ID
Steps: 1. Search each term.
Expected result: Cohen, David is returned for every term.

Title: Search is case-insensitive (API)
Steps: 1. Search each term.
Expected result: Cohen, David is returned for every term.

Title: Lower-case search in the UI finds the offender
Steps: 1. Type "cohen" in the search box.
Expected result: Row "Cohen, David" is shown.

Title: Special characters / no-match search return an empty result
Steps: 1. Search each term.
Expected result: 200, total 0, empty items — wildcards treated literally, no error.

Title: Operator creates a valid offender through the UI
Steps:
1. Click + Add Offender.
2. Fill all fields with valid values (unique national ID).
3. Click Create.
Expected result: 201; toast "Offender created"; row shows the entered values; Offenders and Active counters +1.

Title: API creates a valid offender with 201 and stores it as sent
Steps:
1. POST a valid payload.
2. GET the new id.
Expected result: 201 with id; GET returns the same values.

Title: First name is required (empty / whitespace rejected)
Steps:
1. POST with firstName "".
2. POST with firstName "   ".
Expected result: 400 {"error":"First name is required."}; offender count unchanged.

Title: Last name and national ID are required
Steps:
1. POST with lastName "".
2. POST with nationalId "".
Expected result: 400 with error description; nothing saved.

Title: Duplicate national ID is rejected
Steps:
1. POST a valid payload with nationalId 305412876.
2. Search the ID.
Expected result: 400; only one offender owns the ID.

Title: Date of birth must be a valid date in the past
Steps:
1. POST with dateOfBirth one year in the future.
2. POST with dateOfBirth "not-a-date".
Expected result: 400 for both; nothing saved.

Title: Risk level and status restricted to allowed values
Steps:
1. POST with riskLevel "Critical".
2. POST with status "Deleted".
Expected result: 400 for both.

Title: Empty create form shows a clear error and saves nothing
Steps:
1. Open + Add Offender.
2. Click Create without filling anything.
Expected result: Error banner "First name is required."; modal stays open; count unchanged.

Title: Malformed JSON body returns 400 with an error description
Steps: 1. POST a non-JSON body.
Expected result: 400 with a JSON error description.

Title: Editing one field keeps all untouched fields (incl. risk level)
Steps:
1. Click Edit (form shows High).
2. Change only First name.
3. Save; GET the offender.
Expected result: First name changed; risk level still High; all other fields unchanged.

Title: Changing risk level in the form persists the value shown
URL / endpoint: UI {BASE_URL} Edit → Risk level Medium → Save
Steps:
1. Click Edit.
2. Select Medium.
3. Save; GET the offender.
Expected result: Risk level Medium in list and API.

Title: API PUT with a full valid payload persists every field
Steps:
1. PUT new valid values for all fields.
2. GET the offender.
Expected result: 200; stored values equal the PUT body.

Title: PUT enforces the same validation as create
Steps: 1. PUT with empty first name / future DOB / riskLevel "Extreme" / another offender's national ID.
Expected result: 400 for each; stored record unchanged.

Title: Delete requires confirmation and removes the offender
URL / endpoint: UI {BASE_URL} Delete → confirm dialog → DELETE api/offenders/{id}
Steps:
1. Click Delete, dismiss the prompt.
2. Click Delete, accept the prompt.
Expected result: Prompt names the offender; dismiss keeps the row; accept removes it (toast "Offender deleted").

Title: Deleted offender returns 404 on GET
Steps:
1. DELETE the offender.
2. GET it.

Title: Deleting an offender deletes their trail data
Steps:
1. Delete the offender.
2. Read its trail.
Expected result: No points remain (404 or empty).

Title: DELETE returns 204; repeated DELETE returns 404
Steps: 1. DELETE twice.

Title: Roster dates of birth are DD/MM/YYYY and equal to the stored value
URL / endpoint: UI {BASE_URL} Date of birth column vs GET api/offenders
Steps:
1. Read every DOB on every reachable page.
2. Compare with the API value.

Title: Detail header shows the stored date of birth
Steps:
1. Select Mizrahi, Rachel.
2. Read DOB in the header.

Title: Trail timestamps shown as DD/MM/YYYY HH:mm matching the stored instant
URL / endpoint: UI {BASE_URL} trail table Timestamp column vs GET api/offenders/1/trail
Steps:
1. Select Cohen, David.
2. Compare point #1 timestamp with the API (2026-08-09T11:29Z).
Notes: Also covered indirectly by TC-36 (popup time) and TC-39 (Last seen).

Title: Trail API returns points chronologically
URL / endpoint: GET {BASE_URL}api/offenders/{1..11}/trail; POST 4 points out of order then GET trail
Preconditions: Seeded trails; test offender with 4 points inserted 10:30, 10:00, 10:45, 10:15.
Steps:
1. Read each trail.
2. Compare with timestamp order.
Expected result: Every trail oldest → newest.

Title: Trail table is ordered oldest to newest
Preconditions: Seeded Cohen (16 points, stored out of order).
Steps:
1. Select Cohen, David.
2. Read the # column.
Expected result: Point ids in timestamp order.

Title: Map line runs from the oldest point to the newest point
Steps:
1. Select Cohen, David.
2. Locate the first and last vertex of the line.
3. Match them to markers.
Expected result: Line starts on the oldest point and ends on the newest.
Notes: Visually the line zig-zags across the area.

Title: Map shows one marker per trail point and a trail line
Steps:
1. Select Cohen, David.
2. Count markers and lines.
Expected result: 16 markers, 1 line, title "Trail points (16)".

Title: Clicking a map point shows its recorded data
URL / endpoint: UI {BASE_URL} click marker → popup vs GET api/offenders/1/trail
Steps:
1. Click the first, a middle and the last marker.
2. Compare popup with the API point of the same id.
Expected result: Time, speed (km/h), battery (%), signal (1–5 bars) equal the API values.

Title: A point with an out-of-range signal does not crash the console
Preconditions: Offender with one point signal = 6 (possible because of BUG-14).
Steps: 1. Select the offender.
Expected result: Trail renders; no uncaught error; console stays usable.

Title: Latest reading shows speed/battery/signal of the most recent point
URL / endpoint: UI {BASE_URL} select Cohen → Latest reading vs newest point of GET api/offenders/1/trail
Preconditions: Seeded Cohen; newest point id 1 (11:29Z): 23 km/h, 68%, 1/5.
Steps:
1. Select Cohen, David.
2. Read the card.

Title: Last seen shows the most recent timestamp
Steps:
1. Select Cohen, David.
2. Read Last seen.
Expected result: 09/08/2026, 14:29 (newest point, Asia/Jerusalem).

Title: Operator adds a valid location point through the UI
Steps:
1. Select the offender.
2. + Add location: 32.0901 / 34.7802 / 18.5 / 77 / 4.
3. Click Add.
Expected result: 201; row with these values; Trail points counter +1.

Title: API rejects out-of-range location values
Steps:
1. POST lat ±91 / lon ±181 / speed −1 / battery −1, 101 / signal 0, 6 / lat null, one at a time.
2. Read the trail.
Expected result: 400 with error description for each; trail stays empty.

Title: API accepts valid boundary location values
Steps:
1. POST lat 90 / lon 180 / speed 0 / battery 0 / signal 1.
2. POST lat −90 / lon −180 / battery 100 / signal 5.
Expected result: 201 for both; stored exactly.

Title: UI rejects invalid location values with a visible error
Steps:
1. + Add location with speed −5 and battery 150.
2. Click Add.
Expected result: 400; error message shown; no point added.

Title: Blank speed / battery are not silently saved as 0
Steps:
1. + Add location with only latitude and longitude.
2. Click Add.
Expected result: Rejected with a message.

Title: UI shows an error when the server rejects a location
Steps:
1. + Add location with every field blank.
2. Click Add.
Expected result: Visible error message.

Title: Top-bar counters equal the stats API
URL / endpoint: UI {BASE_URL} top bar vs GET api/stats
Steps:
1. Open the console.
2. Compare counters with the API.
Expected result: Offenders, Active and Trail points equal the API values.

Title: Counters update after creating offenders and points
URL / endpoint: GET api/stats → POST api/offenders ×2 → POST …/locations ×4 → GET api/stats
Steps:
1. Create one Active offender with 4 points and one Inactive offender.
2. Compare stats.
Expected result: +2 offenders, +1 active, +4 points.

Title: Trail-point total drops when an offender with a trail is deleted
URL / endpoint: GET api/stats → DELETE api/offenders/{id} → GET api/stats
Steps:
1. Delete the offender.
2. Compare stats.
Expected result: −1 offender, −4 points.

Title: Offender totals match the stored offenders
Steps:
1. Read stats and the full list.
2. Count total and Active.
Expected result: totalOffenders = list total; activeOffenders = number with status Active.
Notes: totalLocationPoints is NOT consistent (186 reported vs 166 owned) — see BUG-02 / TC-48.

Title: GET unknown offender returns 404
Steps: 1. GET a non-existent id.

Title: Trail of an unknown offender returns 404
Steps: 1. GET the trail of a non-existent id.

Title: PUT / DELETE / POST-location on an unknown offender return 404
Steps: 1. Call each endpoint with a non-existent id.
Expected result: 404 for each.
